resources.string: Lets Gearslip replay touches from the car screen onto the phone while mirroring. Gearslip does not read screen content.
Gearslip is unofficial. No carmaker made or checked it, and it can fail without warning. Set it up before you go, then keep your eyes on the road.
Gearslip uses it to send your music to the car and to hear you when you ask for something or reply to a message. What you say stays on the phone.
The car\'s map and nearby searches need it. Without it, the dashboard shows no map.
The car screen shows your next event. Gearslip only reads your calendar.
The car shows who\'s calling by name, and its Phone app can dial a number or call one of your contacts. Gearslip only reads them.
The first time you plug in, Gearslip offers to pair your phone with the car, so calls play through its speakers.
While Gearslip is connected, it shows a notification with a button to stop. Without this, Android hides it.
The car shows your messages, reads them aloud and lets you reply. Turn Gearslip on in the list this opens.
Android Auto is still installed, and it fights Gearslip for the car\'s USB connection. Disable or uninstall it on the screen this opens.
If your phone asks which app to open when you plug into the car, pick Gearslip and tap Always.
Pick how music reaches the car. Calls go over Bluetooth either way.
Ask for directions, music, or a call by voice. Your phone turns speech into text by itself, and nothing you say leaves it. It needs %1$d MB, downloaded once. Use Wi-Fi if you can.
Run this from a computer with USB debugging on, and Android trusts Gearslip with your audio for good. Without it, you tap Start once each drive.
While audio goes to the car, Android hides what notifications say, as if you were sharing your screen. This lets Gearslip show them during a drive and hide them again after.
Make Gearslip your caller ID app, and the car can answer and decline calls. Without it, calls still ring, but only the phone can answer them.
Pick how the car\'s buttons look. Change it any time in the car\'s settings.
Downloading, %1$d%%. You can carry on; it keeps going.

Turn this on, and Gearslip sends a short note when you open it and after each drive. The note holds no name, account, or location. A random number counts your phone once, and the server keeps no IP address. The notes show which cars work and where the others fail.

Android treats the music Gearslip sends to the car like sharing your screen, so it asks every drive, over a cable or wireless. Over Bluetooth it never asks. You can change this later in Settings.
Or keep the sound going through Gearslip and stop the question for good: plug the phone into a computer with USB debugging on, and run this once.

Android lets an app send other apps\' sound to the car only if it has the microphone permission. It\'s turned off for Gearslip, so music plays on the phone. Turn it on under Permissions, then Microphone.

Through Gearslip sends the phone\'s sound over the car connection, cable or wireless. Android asks to share your screen each drive, and a few apps block it. Bluetooth plays as the phone normally would, and Android never asks.
Gearslip reads each turn aloud through the car\'s speakers, and the music dips while it speaks. Turn it off if your map app\'s own voice already plays in the car.
Listens through the phone\'s own speech service instead of Gearslip\'s. On most phones that\'s Google\'s, which may send your voice to Google. GrapheneOS has none, so Gearslip keeps using its own.
